featured_reviews.name: Rishi Goswami
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Alchemy of the Humble Citadel

There are places in this weary world where the divine is not found in gilded halls, but in the unpretentious gleam of stainless steel, and this small eatery is one such profound discovery. To enter its unassuming doors is to stumble upon a humble citadel of flavor, a corner where the culinary arts reach a state of grace rarely achieved in grander, more self-important establishments.

The menu here is not a scroll of tedious options, but a focused declaration of devotion to the sacred tenets of South Indian cuisine. Consider the Dosa: it arrives not merely as a crisp crepe, but as a vast, golden disc—a perfectly rendered canvas of fermentation and heat, brittle at its edges, yet yielding a warmth at its center that speaks of ancestral knowledge. It is a masterpiece of textural dichotomy.

The accompanying Idli are nothing less than spheres of pure, ethereal manna. They float, cloud-like and impossibly soft, a testament to an alchemy that transforms simple rice and lentil into something buoyant and sublime. And the Vada? A perfectly seasoned, crisp circlet of deep, savory pleasure—hot, intricate, and utterly addictive.

But the true genius of this house resides in the subtleties. The Buttermilk (Chaas) served here is a celestial antidote to the world’s clamor; it is cool, spiced nectar that cleanses the palate and resets the soul, preparing one not just for the next bite, but for the next chapter of life.

The cost of this epicurean journey is perhaps the most bewildering aspect. The price, a mere footnote to the exquisite verse of the meal, suggests either an act of benevolent charity or a complete disregard for modern market dynamics. It defies the greedy gravity that pulls all things toward excess.

In an era defined by chaotic glamour, this small space stands as a quiet reminder: quality is not measured by square footage or chandelier wattage, but by the relentless pursuit of perfection in the small, savory details. Go here to understand that the simplest ingredients, when handled with such uncommon skill and palpable reverence, can deliver one of the richest experiences the human tongue is privileged to know. This is not merely food; it is edible truth.

featured_reviews.name: Dhanashree Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited South Tiffin House, located conveniently near Mira Road railway station, and had a pleasant experience overall.

The restaurant serves good South Indian food, and the quality definitely stands out. The pricing is reasonable—neither too cheap nor too expensive—making it a decent option for a casual meal. The service was nice, and the staff were polite and welcoming, which added to the comfort of the visit.

The place is small and simple, with around four tables available for seating, but it feels cozy rather than crowded. We ordered a cheese sada dosa and a Mysore masala dosa, both of which were tasty and well-prepared. As a beverage, we also had garam badam milk, which was a nice and comforting addition.

Overall, it was a good experience, especially if you’re looking for satisfying South Indian food near the station.

I ordered food from Oota Thindi, Borivali West, and was extremely disappointed by the excessive amount of oil used in the dish. The curry was literally floating in oil, making it unpleasant to eat and raising serious health concerns.

Traditional food does not mean food should be drenched in oil. Such cooking practices are unsafe for regular consumption, especially for customers mindful of cholesterol, heart health, and overall well-being. The taste was completely overpowered by oil, and a large portion had to be discarded.

Restaurants have a responsibility towards their customers’ health. I genuinely hope Oota Thindi takes this feedback seriously and improves its cooking standards. Until then, I would strongly advise the restaurant to control oil usage and maintain healthier food quality.

featured_reviews.name: Raj Arunachala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Classic example of how great food can be ruined by absolutely horrific service!

Oota Thindi, serving Pan South Indian cuisine is a sure-shot candidate for one of those restaurant makeover shows!

From the get go, the reservation process starts off in confusion. The person managing the front desk is absolutely clueless about taking reservations and then subsequently calling people. I kept a tab on him that’s why I was able to get a table!

Having arrived at the table, the waiting staff is completely clueless. It took a really long time before someone came to take order. Our waiter was knowledgeable about the menu though. And made some great suggestions.

The menu is another disaster with too many options that most people aren’t even familiar with. Even being a south Indian who lives in Tamil Nadu, some of menu items were confusing. A simple classification of Starters, Main course etc is preferred.

We ordered some starters which arrived on time. As for the rest of our courses, the wait time was painstakingly long. The waiters have no clue what’s going on with orders. And there are too many of them mulling around avoiding talking to customers.

So many other customers were also getting frustrated by the delays. One person even yelled at the manager! Though he just shrugged it off and walked away!

The food is the only redeeming factor as is the nicely done ambience. Although the main hall is too brightly lit for dinner.

I find myself reluctant to recommend this place despite the good food because of the appalling service! How is it so hard in Mumbai?!
Just hire some very capable Shetty people who have mastered the art of running a South Indian restaurant!

Overall, a very disappointing experience at Oota Thindi!

featured_reviews.name: shripad marathe
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Oota Thindi and had an absolutely wonderful dining experience that I just had to share!

I ordered a variety of dishes that showcased the authentic flavors of South Indian cuisine, and each one was a treat:

Benne Ellu Podi Dosa (INR 290) - This was the star of my meal! The butter and sesame powder combination created such a rich, nutty flavor that perfectly complemented the crispy dosa. Absolutely divine!

Thali (INR 695 )-  An excellent value for money! The thali was well-portioned with a great variety of dishes that gave me a complete taste of traditional South Indian flavors.

Thenga Manga Sundal (INR 225) - A refreshing and healthy option with coconut and raw mango. The tanginess was just right, making it a perfect side dish.

Thakali Thokku Brahmin Style Idli (INR 225 ) - Soft, fluffy idlis paired with the flavorful tomato thokku. This Brahmin-style preparation was authentic and delicious!

Kalyana Rasam (INR 245 ) - The wedding-style rasam was aromatic and soul-warming. Perfect comfort food!

The total came to INR 1,780 , which I found very reasonable considering the quality and quantity of food. The ordering system was modern and user-friendly, and the service was efficient.

If you're craving authentic South Indian cuisine, Oota Thindi is definitely the place to go. I'll definitely be returning to try more items from their menu!

Highly recommended! 👌

featured_reviews.name: Kiran Dixit
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Oota Thindi in Borivali West for their unlimited South Indian breakfast. Since it was a weekday morning, the place wasn’t crowded—though I did notice a Marathi actress at one of the tables, which was a pleasant surprise.
The décor and ambiance are thoughtfully done, with colors and symbols that reflect the essence of South India. The food overall was decent. I especially enjoyed the Pongal rice, dal vada, and their signature filter coffee. The chutneys were fresh and flavorful, and the pineapple sheera was a delightful sweet ending.
On the flip side, the idlis could have been softer and the medu vada (Ulundu) crispier. The sambar was served lukewarm initially, but when I requested a hot one, the staff promptly obliged—which speaks well of their service.
Overall, Oota Thindi is worth a visit if you want to relish authentic South Indian flavors in Borivali.
